subject: Learning Methods
title: Step Two: Identify the Gaps
description: A 60-second lesson on Step Two: Identify the Gaps.

hook.text: After writing your explanation, you notice the sentences that trail off, the analogies that break, the logic that jumps.

buildup.text: Each faltering point is a knowledge gap. Circle or highlight every place where your explanation became vague or wrong.

discovery.text: These gaps are the most valuable part of the process. They show you exactly what to study next, saving time.

twist.text: Without this step, people study everything equally. With it, they focus effort on the 20 percent they actually need.

climax.text: Return to your sources and study only the circled gaps. Then rewrite those sections of your explanation.

punchline.text: Gaps are gold. Study only what you couldn't explain.

quiz.question: Why does identifying gaps in your explanation make studying more efficient?
options: It reduces total reading time to zero
It focuses effort on the specific areas you don't understand
Gaps indicate material that won't appear on the exam
